title: Streamline audit log search + bulk-download workflow with query presets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Admins need a faster, safer way to search across the console audit stream and produce bulk downloads for compliance review. Current flow requires several manual steps, often returns large unwieldy CSVs, and lacks fine-grained visibility tied to RBAC v2 and org-level presets. This ticket implements a server-driven search+download workflow with saved query presets, streaming JSON Lines and CSV options, role-aware visibility, and safeguards for PII and SSO/SAML identity fields.

Goals:
- Provide fast, cursored search with predictable memory and latency for large time ranges.
- Offer streaming bulk-download (ndjson and chunked CSV) so the browser can start writing to disk before the entire query completes.
- Persist user/team query presets; allow org admins to mark presets as shared or private.
- Enforce RBAC v2 visibility rules on log fields and exportability (redact or omit fields per role).
- Surface export usage and sampling metrics in Console Optimize dashboards.

Constraints and non-goals:
- Not changing retention policy in this ticket.
- Not creating a new compliance archive format; we support CSV and JSON Lines only.

High-level design:
1) API: POST /v1/audit/search?download=true returns a 202 with a download job id. The job executes server-side using a streaming cursor over the time-indexed audit store. The client receives a streaming presigned URL (or SSE/WS updates) and partial download chunks.
2) Pagination: Server provides stable, opaque cursor tokens for paging search results; cursors are time-and-offset aware to avoid duplicates during concurrent writes. UI will use continuous scrolling for preview and an explicit \"Create Download\" button for bulk exports.
3) Export formats: ndjson (recommended) and CSV (legacy). CSV generation will emit a header row with canonical column order; fields that are conditionally redacted will have a placeholder value \"[REDACTED]\".
4) Query presets: Save arbitrary filter+column configurations as presets. Presets have metadata: name, visibility (private/team/org), created_by, last_used. Admins can pin presets for their org and restrict who can export using that preset.
5) RBAC/SSO integration: On job submission, the service evaluates RBAC v2 rules and the user's SAML attributes (if present) to produce an effective export policy. Fields requiring system-level access (e.g., full_auth_header, raw_token) must be redacted unless the requesting principal is an org-owner with explicit export_privilege.
6) Safety: Add a server-side preflight that estimates result size and rejects or requires additional confirmation for exports larger than 50M rows or 10GB. Jobs over that threshold must be approved by an admin role and will be queued in the offline export tier.
7) Telemetry and auditing: Each download job creates an audit entry with job_id, requester, preset_id (if any), filters, size_estimate, and final delivered_byte_count. Exports themselves are tracked for cost/billing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Users can perform focused searches and page through results with stable cursors.
- Users can create a download job and begin streaming ndjson to the browser before the job completes.
- Presets can be created, edited, shared, and deleted; visibility enforces org/team boundaries.
- RBAC v2 enforced: users see only fields permitted by their role; exports respect the same constraints.
- The preflight size check triggers and requires admin confirmation when thresholds are exceeded.
- Audit entries for export jobs appear in the audit store and are queryable by admin roles.

Implementation notes:
- Backend: extend audit-query-service with a DownloadJob worker. Use Kafka for job status updates to the console. Use cursor design similar to KV-cache cursors but include time boundaries.
- Storage: stream results from the primary parquet-backed audit store; for very large exports write to S3 in parts and serve a presigned manifest.
- UX: Add an inline \"Export\" CTA on search results; a modal to select format, preset, and confirm thresholds. Add a \"Saved queries\" panel in the left rail with filter previews.
- Security: hook into RBAC v2 decision service to get effective field-level permissions. Ensure SAML attributes (e.g., saml:org_role) are validated against current SSO mapping.
- Performance: prove that a 30 day query with 5M events can be scanned and a 100k row preview returned under 2s for common filters (time + actor + route).

Out-of-scope followups: scheduled recurring exports, compressed archive packaging, and cross-org aggregated exports.
acceptance_criteria: Cursored search returns stable pages with no duplicates under concurrent writes
CreateDownload API accepts filters and returns a job_id and estimated size
Streaming ndjson starts delivering chunks within 3s of job start for small-to-medium queries
Saved query presets persist visibility and can be shared by org-admins
RBAC v2 redaction rules applied to preview and final exports
Preflight size estimate blocks very large exports and requires admin approval
qa_steps: 1) Sign in as a regular member, run a 7-day audit search, verify preview loads and paging works
2) Create a private preset, reload console, verify only you see it
3) Org-admin creates a shared preset and pins it; member can use but cannot delete
4) Submit a CreateDownload job for ndjson; interrupt network and resume using job_id; verify partial file contains valid ndjson lines
5) Attempt export with a user lacking export_privilege and validate sensitive fields are redacted
6) Trigger preflight by selecting a wide time range and confirm admin approval flow

notes: Edge case to watch: when RBAC role changes mid-job (user demoted) we must decide whether to continue the job with original permissions or cancel and log. Current plan: snapshot effective permissions at job creation and re-evaluate on deliver for compliance exports.
implementation_todo: Implement server-side redaction module and integrate with RBAC decision service
Update Console saved queries panel to include visibility controls
risks: Large exports could increase S3 egress costs if not rate-limited
Redaction rules mismatch could leak fields if RBAC mapping is inconsistent
Long-running jobs need lifecycle (retry/cleanup) to avoid resource leakage
